brief: Owner's direction: two sign-in journeys (Jellyfin parity; OIDC with a TV code or QR approved on a signed-in device), same behaviour after sign-in. Four questions: the framing, a device-authorization grant in JS-039, account mapping, priority.
tradeoff: Given up by viewers: a QR on the TV. Unmodified Jellyfin TV apps draw Quick Connect's six digits, and none starts a device-authorization grant, so that endpoint would serve no supported client. Given up by operators: removing someone at the provider stops new sign-ins only, and issued tokens run until the user is disabled in jellyscale. Also given up: group-driven roles and libraries, and a second provider.
entry: Framing accepted. 'Same' means either journey ends in an ordinary per-device token, sent on every media request (D-026) and never in a cookie (invariant 63). Session, device list, watch state, library access (JS-036) and revocation (JS-033) follow the jellyscale user, never the journey. No device-authorization grant: Quick Connect is the TV journey for both account kinds, a code on the TV approved from a device signed in by password or provider. Mapping in scope: one provider declared in configuration, identity as issuer plus subject; a first sign-in links the local user whose name equals the provider's username claim, keeping watch state, as migrated users without passwords arrive; provisioning a default-policy viewer is a configuration switch, off by default. Mapping out: linking by email, groups to administrator or libraries, an admission group (the provider's application policy does it), several providers, provider logout or session expiry ending tokens. JS-039 stays one task, directly after JS-178 and ahead of JS-056. Reopens on a client that authorizes every media request drawing a QR or shipping the grant (BL-229, then a brief); an operator report of provider offboarding not cutting access, of a provider that cannot limit who uses the application, or of two providers in use.
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'A password, a code entered on the TV from a phone, or the household's own single sign-on, and only the libraries they are allowed to see'; goal 3, 'Current Jellyfin clients that authorize every request work unmodified'; the non-goal 'A client that works only with jellyscale'; invariant 63. Owner, 2026-11-22: nothing outruns the product.
